items.guidance: Check the Express route files for an existing health or status route. If you add one, register the GET /health handler early in the app setup, before the routers, auth middleware, and any custom-domain redirect, and do not call Redis or the database from it.

Open server/redis.js and check whether the Cluster client is always created or only when a setting (for example a cluster flag or a list of cluster nodes) is present, and whether a single-node ioredis client path exists. Report the setting and value that select a single-node client. If the Cluster client is unconditional, report the file and the modules that import it.

Find the Bull queues and their process handlers, and check whether they use the client from server/redis.js. Report whether the file that npm start runs registers the processors or a separate file does, with its exact command. Also report the Redis variable names that Bull reads, so the vendor can map them to REDIS_URL.
